facts.text: McLemoresville is the birthplace and final resting place of television star Dixie Carter and her husband, actor Hal Holbrook.
Bethel College, Tennessee’s only four‑year liberal arts school founded by the Cumberland Presbyterian Church, began its campus in McLemoresville before moving to McKenzie.
In the mid‑1800s, McLemoresville boasted more than eleven saloons and several boarding schools, including the Collegiate Institute and Women’s Collegiate Institute.
The town once served as Carroll County’s seat and was the county’s largest community before the railroad bypassed it in the 19th century.
Locals affectionately call McLemoresville “McLey,” a nickname that echoes the town’s historic pronunciation.
The McLemoresville Activities Center, known locally as the “MAC,” hosts community events in a building that once housed the town’s high school.
